title: Building a Shopping List
story: Your roommate texts: 'Pick up milk, eggs, bread, and butter.' You need to organize this into a proper shopping list with numbers so you can check items off as you go through the store.
why: Combining Vec operations — push, len, and for loops — into a complete mini-application teaches practical collection usage.
analogy: A shopping list Vec is like a paper checklist at the store. You write items down (push), read them in order (for/while), and cross them off (pop) as you find them. The paper grows with your list and shrinks as you shop.
try_it: Add a quantity to each item by storing `"2x milk"` instead of just `"milk"`. Add a way to search for an item: loop through the list and print 'Found!' when you match. Add a `remove_item` function that takes an index and removes that item — but be careful with how removal shifts the rest of the Vec.
tips: Use `i + 1` to convert from 0-based index (computers) to 1-based counting (humans)
A while loop gives you the index, which a for loop doesn't — choose based on what you need
Break larger tasks into functions: `print_list`, `add_item`, `remove_item` each do one thing
common_mistakes: Printing `i` directly as the item number — that gives 0, 1, 2 instead of 1, 2, 3
Forgetting to increment `i` in the while loop — results in an infinite loop on the first item
Using `for item in list` when you need the index — for loops give values, not positions
